html:
Trần Hưng Đạo was a Vietnamese prince and the commander of the armies of Đại Việt who defeated two Mongol invasions in the 1280s. He is one of the great heroes of Vietnamese history.

He was a nephew of the first emperor of the Trần dynasty. The Yuan empire of Kublai Khan invaded Đại Việt in 1258, 1285 and 1287 to 1288; see Mongol invasions of Vietnam. Against vastly larger armies he used delay and harassment: he abandoned the capital, let the enemy wear itself out in heat and disease, cut its supply lines and struck when it pulled back.

In 1288 he won his most famous victory at the Bạch Đằng River, repeating the trick of the battle of 938: iron tipped stakes in the riverbed caught the Mongol fleet as the tide fell. His proclamation to his officers, urging them to fight, is still taught in schools. Many Vietnamese worship him as a saint, and temples to him stand across the country.
sum: Trần Hưng Đạo was a Vietnamese prince and the commander of the armies of Đại Việt who defeated two Mongol invasions in the 1280s. He is one of the great heroes of Vietnamese history.
